note: THE SHARED FIXTURES. One set of cases, read by all five sides so they cannot drift: the server's clean (tulmi/src/experience/native/clean.ts), the phone's cleanNativeLooks (src/native/looksCore.ts), the iOS decode and clamp (NLookModel.swift), the Android planner (NLookPlan.kt) and the keyboard's face drawers. A case is a design, a face or a path with the verdict every side must reach. If two sides disagree on a case, the case is the referee, not either implementation.

verdicts.ok: Passes clean unchanged. Every node and key survives.
verdicts.clamped: Passes, but something inside is dropped or capped. `keep` says what must still be there; `drop` says what must be gone.
verdicts.dropped: The whole design (or face) is refused. The REST of the catalog is kept: one bad design never refuses the catalog.
verdicts.skipped: Not refused, just not for this build: its format is higher than the build draws. It is skipped alone and the server never names it.

files.what: Widget designs: the good ones, every structural limit edge, unknown nodes and style keys, a format that is too new, Android nesting and expansion. A case may also carry a `bar` block (the data to draw it against and the stage names each renderer must draw, with their roles), which is how the one Bar rule is settled.
Live Activity designs and ContentState bodies: region node caps, the 3.5 KB body guard, vars clamping, the lenient decode of old and new JSON.
Bind paths: known, unknown, sensitive on a lock or accessory root, vars.* on a lock root, Each over a list, words and their slots on each surface, templates and the hide rule.
The M L Q C Z O path grammar: valid paths, a C path from the animation format, an unknown command, an over-long d.
Keyboard faces and skins: a valid face, a mark with a path shape, press kinds, the budgets, and the things a skin may never carry.

rules: Unknown degrades, never throws: an unknown node draws its `fallback`, then nothing; an unknown style key is ignored; an unknown colour becomes `ink`.
A design whose `format` is too new is skipped ALONE. The catalog around it is served as usual.
Every limit in shared/types/nlook.ts NLOOK_LIMITS is checked three times: on publish, on the phone before writing, and in native code before drawing.
A drop is never a crash and never a blank widget: the chain is the node's fallback, then the design's `fallback` design, then today's hand-written native view.
A word's own slots ({n}, {stage}, {of}) are filled only by WORD_SLOTS in shared/types/nlook.ts. A word with a slot this surface cannot fill resolves to EMPTY, so a raw "{n}" never prints.
A Text hides when EVERY slot in it resolved empty, punctuation and all. One empty slot of two does not hide a Text that still has words.

`Bar` draws one segment per stage with `of` clamped to 1-8, and puts the stage names under it ONLY when `segments` resolves to exactly `of` names: the done ones `meta`, the current one bold in `ink`, the rest `dim`. Any other count draws segments alone.
A palette scheme may leave `dim`, `outline` and `hollow` out. ROLE_FALLBACK resolves them (meta, line, line) rather than losing the node.

`align` is ACROSS the stack: on V it is leading/center/trailing, on H it is top/center/bottom, by box and never by text baseline. On Z it is both axes at once. Spacing ALONG a stack is `gap` and `Spacer` only, so the only values are start, center and end; anything else is refused at publish and drawn as `start` on a phone.
